title: The Medical Segmentation Decathlon

false_alarm.note: Caused by the checker: the per-dataset targets (17 in total) are in a table of the cited data paper, and the checker's text of cited papers omits table contents.
The cited LiTS paper lists IRCAD in France as a data source and describes the LiTS data used for the Decathlon's liver task; the hospital's full name is a detail, not a misattribution.
The cited paper describes an 'unmanageable number of research papers' and about 12,000 studies building on U-Net since 2015, i.e. thousands per year; the not-found verdict is too literal.

debatable.note: The checker read the 2019 arXiv preprint ('29 out of 49'); the sentence cites the 2021 Nature Methods version, whose updated results likely contain the 33-of-53 figure. The BraTS 2020 win is not in the preprint either. Version mismatch, not verifiable here.
The preprint the checker read says the KiTS top-15 were U-Net offspring but gives no count of nnU-Net derivatives; the journal version may. Same version mismatch.
The GlaS paper says malignant gland boundaries are not well defined and that inter-observer variability was not measured; 'experts often do not agree' is a stretch, cited jointly with another work.
The source says 70% of challenge tasks were segmentation; the sentence says 70% of challenges. A real but minor imprecision (challenges can have several tasks).
The sentence describes the citing paper's own challenge; the citation most plausibly supports the notion of a challenge 'task', which the cited meta-analysis defines, not the MSD details.

summary_line: Caught 6 of 6 planted errors · 3 false alarms
